data.name: Reuen
data.gender_notes: Reuen is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name 'Ruwach', meaning 'wind' or 'exalted one'. In the Bible, Reuben is the name of the firstborn son of Jacob and Leah. The name Reuben can be translated as 'Behold, a son' or 'Returning'. As the firstborn son, Reuben was to be the one who would receive the birthright and the blessing from his father. However, he failed to live up to this responsibility and his position was taken by Joseph. Despite this, Reuben remained loyal to his brother and helped him when he was sold into slavery in Egypt.
data.etymology: Reuen belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Return.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Reuen total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name symbolizes spiritual guidance, care, and leadership, resonating with Christian values of protection and nurturing.

data.cultural_impact: The name Reuben holds cultural significance as a Hebrew name. According to Jewish tradition, a child's Hebrew name is significant in determining their future and identity. The name Reuben is rooted in ancient biblical history and represents the firstborn son of a prominent biblical figure. It is a name that carries cultural weight and is often associated with leadership and heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Reuben has spiritual significance as a reminder of God's grace and mercy toward His people. Despite Reuben's failure to live up to his birthright and position as the firstborn son, God still chose him to be a part of His plan. It highlights the importance of humility, forgiveness, and redemption. Reuben's name is a testament to God's unending love and His willingness to give us a second chance, no matter what we have done in our past.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Reuen, meaning "seen by God" in Hebrew, symbolizes the belief that every life is observed and cared for by the divine presence. This name is a reminder of God's love and watchfulness, instilling a sense of connection and faith in the bearer.

historical_references.reference: The Golden Legend, 'Reuen, the son of Amalric, was a young man of noble birth who dedicated himself to Christ, and, refusing to be married as his father bade him, he was cast into a dungeon. There he lived in the greatest poverty and penance until he was set at liberty by the death of his father.'
historical_references.context: A hagiography account of a Christian martyr named Reuen who resisted his father's commands to marry and was consequently imprisoned. He lived in penance until his father died, freeing him.
